tldr: Team reviewed how to respond to a customer (Manhattan WMS user) whose SFTP automation was quoted at four-plus weeks of discovery. The in-house Selector-based replacement for Dispatch Cloud may remove the need for it.

Harry demoed the platform: drag-and-drop CSV import, bulk pack and dispatch, Dispatch Cloud-style file layout, shipping-method mapping, a Manhattan export, browser printing with no QZ Tray, and an SFTP/API upload endpoint.
Gaps raised: per-order package count in the CSV, SKU-level commodity data for later cross-border, and how benches and users link to printers. Testing so far is light.
Whether to demo to the customer today was left open. The plan is to run live tests first, then decide between a demo and booking a smaller session.
decisions: Hide the API key setup from the customer for now, but keep the API running in the background.
Use the drag-and-drop CSV import as the answer to the customer's SFTP automation ask, subject to testing.
Do a proper end-to-end test against the live Selector account before deciding whether to demo on the customer call.
Weights will be importable in pounds, with units in centimetres and pounds, so the customer no longer converts them.

actions.text: Get the requested changes through and drop a note to Speaker 1 when they are ready.
Send Phil credits for the platform so they can test the flow, and check the bench/user printer workflow is the intended one.
Run end-to-end tests against the live Selector account (deleting test orders afterwards) once Harry's changes are in, ideally before the customer call.
Confirm whether shipping methods pass route codes to Selector so contracts can be configured per mapping.
Email Geeta asking for a 30-minute demo slot, only once the team agrees to demo.
Run a real label print test from home on their printer.
Ask John about the FedEx tracking scan-time and time zone handling.
Set up an hour-long session with Phil, Chris and the team to run a pseudo customer process and find where to streamline.
Check the CSV export file type used for the Manhattan export.

questions: Should the team demo to the customer on today's call, or book a smaller session? Geeta wants a large audience.
Should the CSV support a declared package count per order, instead of one row per product? That is a fundamental format change, so the team plans to ask the customer.
How will SKU-level commodity data be kept for future cross-border (Canada) shipping?
Are printers tied to a packing bench or a user, and when does a user pick a bench?
Can the platform manifest as Dispatch Cloud does, or does it only auto-commit to Selector?
Can an order hold two references (reference and consignment reference), so the container ID can be imported?
Do FedEx tracking scan times need the time zone ignored and the local time treated as a string?
Does printing from the browser work on the customer's real label printers? It has not been tested.
